t: Length of the Longest Subsequence That Sums to Target
o: Classic 0/1-knapsack variant where the 'value' being maximized is the item count. All numbers are positive and target <= 1000, so a DP over achievable sums fits easily: dp[s] = maximum number of elements forming a subsequence with sum exactly s. Order of elements is irrelevant for subsequences here since we only care about multiset sums.
k: dp[s] = max count of items achieving sum s; process items one by one like 0/1 knapsack.
Iterate sums downward so each item is used at most once.
All nums[i] >= 1 keeps the reachable-sum space bounded by target.

a.i: Initialize dp[0]=0 and dp[s>0]=-infinity (unreachable). For each num, update dp[s] = max(dp[s], dp[s-num]+1) iterating s from high to low. The answer is dp[target], or -1 if unreachable.
s: Create dp array of size target+1, dp[0]=0, others -1 sentinel.
For each num, loop s from target down to num.
dp[s] = max(dp[s], dp[s-num] + 1) when dp[s-num] is reachable.
a.t: O(n * target) — about 1e6 operations at the limits.

w: The downward sum loop is essential — upward iteration would allow reusing an item multiple times (unbounded knapsack). Using -1 as 'unreachable' avoids needing infinity. Edge case: target 0 would give 0 (empty subsequence), though constraints guarantee target >= 1. Follow-up: reconstruct the actual subsequence by storing parent pointers.
